learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the rules for changing singular nouns to plural nouns, including regular, irregular, and special spelling rules.]
warm_up_hook: 📖 What happens when you have one chocolate, but then your friend gives you three more? You now have chocolate**s**! Let's explore the magic rules of making words jump from 'Just One' (Singular) to 'Many' (Plural)!

lesson_modules.teaching_content: The most common way to make a plural is by adding '-s'. However, if a word ends in s, ss, sh, ch, x, or o, we usually add '-es' to make it plural.
examples_or_templates: Add -es: bus -> buses, box -> boxes, potato -> potatoes, watch -> watches

lesson_modules.teaching_content: If a word ends in a consonant + 'y', drop the 'y' and add '-ies'. If it ends in 'f' or 'fe', we usually change the 'f' or 'fe' to '-ves'.
examples_or_templates: Change 'y' to 'ies': baby -> babies, city -> cities
Change 'f/fe' to 'ves': leaf -> leaves, knife -> knives

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Some nouns are rule-breakers! They change their spelling completely, or sometimes they don't change at all when they become plural.
examples_or_templates: Spelling Change: man -> men, child -> children, tooth -> teeth, mouse -> mice
No Change: sheep -> sheep, deer -> deer, fish -> fish

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ What is the correct plural form of 'Lady'?
❓ Which of these words remains the exact same in both singular and plural forms?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the plural forms of 'Hero' and 'Glass'.
subjective_practice.hint: Both of these words follow the '-es' rule! Look at their ending letters.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Rewrite this sentence by changing the bold noun to plural: 'The **child** is playing in the park.'
subjective_practice.hint: The plural form of 'child' is an irregular plural that ends in '-ren'.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Write the plural of 'Thief'.
subjective_practice.hint: Words ending in 'f' usually drop the 'f' and add '-ves'.

activity_or_assignment.title: 🛒 The Grocery List Challenge
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Ask your parents to show you the weekly grocery list. Rewrite it by changing all the singular items into plurals (e.g., 1 Onion -> 5 Onions, 1 Loaf of bread -> 2 Loaves of bread).

chapter_summary: ⭐ Singular means exactly one; Plural means more than one.
⭐ Most nouns form plurals by simply adding -s or -es.
⭐ Words ending in 'y' often change to '-ies', and 'f/fe' often change to '-ves'.
⭐ Irregular nouns change their spelling completely (mouse -> mice) or stay exactly the same (sheep -> sheep).
